configurePresets.name: linux-clang-asan
configurePresets.description: #213. The fuzz targets carry -fsanitize=fuzzer,address,undefined, so this is their natural lane, and tier1's matrix selects lanes purely by preset name with no per-lane -D overrides -- a workflow flag would be the special case here, not the preset. It also keeps local reproduction of the CI lane accurate. COSTS: this adds one build+link per fuzz target and one fast ctest per corpus; measured small against the lane's own build, but a MEASUREMENT ROTS so re-derive rather than trusting a number here -- `cmake --build build/linux-clang-asan --target $(ninja -C build/linux-clang-asan -t targets | grep -o '^fuzz_[a-z_]*' | tr '\n' ' ')` for build cost, `ctest --test-dir build/linux-clang-asan -L fuzz` for replay cost, `du -ch build/linux-clang-asan/bin/fuzz_*` for disk. No existing object's command line changes, so no compiler-cache entry is invalidated -- that one is STRUCTURAL and does not rot. ⚠️ DISK IS THE AXIS TO WATCH: this is the disk-tightest leg in the matrix and it has died with `ld: final link failed: No space left on device` before, so if that recurs the fuzz binaries are one of the things to weigh. ASYMMETRY, deliberate: linux-clang-libc++-asan does NOT set FIXPP_BUILD_FUZZ. One lane replaying the corpora is the regression guard #213 asked for; a second would duplicate the cost without covering any additional seed.

testPresets.name: linux-clang-asan
testPresets.description: ASan. jobs=4 — #267, same-VM A-B-A in run 33977674899: j=1 1252.4 s -> j=4 578.4 s, wall 2.17x, achieved concurrency 3.01x. Peak RSS 2.17 -> 3.32 GiB, 21.3% of a 15.61 GiB runner. ⚠️ THE TWO SERIAL PASSES DISAGREE BY 6.3%, above the 5% tolerance, so this sample would VOID on that alone even after the cleanliness fix — of the five widened lanes this one's speedup is the least trustworthy, and it wants its own re-dispatch before the number is repeated. ⚠️ NOT a clean `MEASURED` figure: run 33977674899's verdict was FORMALLY REJECTED (a source-tree-cleanliness failure in every pass of every lane, since fixed). The wall times are still same-VM and comparable — the verdict is void, not the clock. ⚠️ Wall speedup and achieved concurrency are DIFFERENT numbers; do not quote one as the other. ⚠️ This lane is NOT on any tier's critical path, so it buys no TIER time — applied on the explicit 2026-09-05 decision to widen the measured lanes and observe, which is a different and stated basis. testPresets.name: linux-clang-ubsan
testPresets.description: UBSan. jobs=4 — #267 phase 2, MEASURED 1.79x (1993 -> 1114 s, ~14.6 min/run) by a PAIRED same-VM run, cross-validated on a second VM to 1.9%/4.2%. Peak 0.65 -> 0.86 GiB, 5.5% of a 15.61 GiB runner. ⚠️ Do NOT copy to another lane without ITS OWN paired measurement: between-VM wall-clock variance is 27-43%, so only a paired same-VM run can decide a lane. debug was separately confirmed at 2.10x; tsan's j=2-vs-j=4 question is UNRESOLVED (its comparison was unpaired). See ci/ctest-parallelism-probe.md. || #268 — UBSAN_OPTIONS BELONGS HERE, NOT IN THE WORKFLOW. UBSan's default mode is RECOVERABLE: a finding prints 'runtime error:', execution continues, and the process exits 0 — so this lane ran the whole suite for its entire existence and could not go red on a UBSan finding, while /speckit-verify set halt_on_error=1 BY HAND at every gate. That asymmetry between CI and local IS the defect, so the fix is put where both read it: a testPresets environment reaches ctest and ctest passes it to every test, so CI, a developer's `ctest --preset`, and /speckit-verify all now get the same behaviour from one place — where a workflow `env:` would have fixed CI and left the asymmetry intact. Proven by a paired local A/B on one binary (2026-08-18, clang-22): the same signed-overflow test PASSES with ctest exiting 0 without this environment, and FAILS with it, print_stacktrace=1 yielding a real frame list. ⚠️ A preset environment value OVERRIDES the inherited one, so a hand-set UBSAN_OPTIONS no longer composes with it — add options here rather than around the invocation.

testPresets.name: linux-clang-tsan
testPresets.description: TSan. jobs=2 — a CONSERVATIVE DEFAULT, not a measured optimum. ⚠️ The j=2-vs-j=4 comparison was made across TWO SEPARATE RUNS on a lane whose between-VM wall-clock spread is 43.3% (1903/2160/1376 s at an unchanged j=2), so it resolves nothing and an earlier claim of 'no gain at j=4' is WITHDRAWN. What IS solid: peak RSS reproduces to <2%, so j=4's +36% memory is real, and debug/ubsan both gain ~1.8-2.1x when measured properly. Settle this with the same paired A-B-A design before changing it.

testPresets.name: linux-clang-coverage
testPresets.description: Coverage. jobs=4 — #267, same-VM A-B-A in run 33977674899: j=1 1280.3 s -> j=4 663.8 s, wall 1.93x, achieved concurrency 2.51x — the lowest parallel efficiency of the five, which is expected given per-test profile writing. Peak RSS 0.87 -> 1.06 GiB, 6.8% of a 15.61 GiB runner. The two serial passes agree to 2.5%. ⚠️ THE COVERAGE MECHANISM IS INTACT AT j=4 AND THE COVERAGE CONTENT IS NOT STABLE AT ANY j — two separate facts, measured in run 33977674899. Mechanism: all three passes report status=ok with profraw_count=367, so the per-PID LLVM_PROFILE_FILE scheme (%p, set as a step-level override by tier1's coverage job) loses no profile when four test binaries run at once. Content: the two SERIAL passes produced DIFFERENT merged coverage (17886 vs 17882 lines, different digests) at UNCHANGED concurrency, so this suite has run-to-run coverage nondeterminism of its own and #267 acceptance item 4 CANNOT be attributed to --parallel from this sample in either direction — the baseline moves. The j=4 pass read 17877, i.e. within the same order as the 4-line serial-to-serial gap (~0.05% of 17.9k covered lines). Do not read that as 'parallel loses coverage', and do not read this preset as having established the opposite. The nondeterminism is pre-existing, is NOT caused by this widening, and wants its own issue. ⚠️ NOT a clean `MEASURED` figure: run 33977674899's verdict was FORMALLY REJECTED (a source-tree-cleanliness failure in every pass of every lane, since fixed). The wall times are still same-VM and comparable — the verdict is void, not the clock. ⚠️ Wall speedup and achieved concurrency are DIFFERENT numbers; do not quote one as the other. ⚠️ This lane is NOT on any tier's critical path, so it buys no TIER time — applied on the explicit 2026-09-05 decision to widen the measured lanes and observe, which is a different and stated basis. All three caveats are written out ONCE, with the reasoning, in research/G19-fix-fpml-iso20022/decisions/speckit/267-widening-decisions.md §1-§3 — corrected there, not in five preset descriptions.

testPresets.name: linux-clang-libc++-tsan
testPresets.description: libc++ TSan. jobs=4 — #267, and THE ONLY WIDENING IN THIS SET THAT BUYS TIER TIME. This lane is Tier 3's critical path (87 min against a next-longest 44), and on #267's criterion a tier costs what its SLOWEST lane costs. Same-VM A-B-A in run 33977674899: j=1 4656.1 s -> j=4 2521.6 s -> j=1 4634.8 s, wall 1.84x, achieved concurrency 2.82x — about 35 minutes off the tier's bound. ⚠️ THE BEST-EVIDENCED SAMPLE OF THE SEVEN: the two serial passes agree to 0.5% (tolerance 5%), /proc/stat steal was +0 across all three intervals, calibration drift 0.5%/1.4%, all 357 tests ran in every pass matching ci/expected-eligible-tests.txt, and sanitizer reports were 0 throughout. Peak RSS 0.96 -> 1.93 GiB (+100%), 12.4% of a 15.61 GiB runner. Summed test time +53%, which is a DISCLOSURE and not an objection — runner-minutes is the axis #267 deprioritises. ⚠️ THIS DOES NOT CONTRADICT linux-clang-tsan BEING LEFT AT jobs=2, and the reason is the BASELINE, not the sanitizer: that lane's inconclusive comparison was j=2 -> j=4, this one is j=1 -> j=4. Going from serial to four is a different question from going from two to four, and only the first is answered here. ⚠️ NOT A CLEAN `MEASURED` FIGURE: that run's verdict was FORMALLY REJECTED because every pass of every lane failed fixpp::dict::codegen-build-graph-check — the driver wrote its sample into the checkout (since fixed). The failure cost 0.03-0.71 s and hit all three passes identically, so the wall times stay same-VM and comparable; the verdict is void on comparability, not on the clock. See research/G19-fix-fpml-iso20022/decisions/speckit/267-widening-decisions.md.

testPresets.name: windows-msvc-asan
testPresets.description: MSVC ASan. jobs=4 — #267, and THE MATRIX'S CRITICAL PATH. This lane bounds Tier 2 and through it PR feedback time, so on #267's criterion — a tier costs what its SLOWEST lane costs — it is the one widening with the largest reach. Campaign run 33990959916, the FIRST VALID sample this lane has ever produced: j=1 4307.4 s -> j=4 2147.3 s -> j=1 4277.3 s, wall 2.00x, achieved concurrency 3.07x, A-vs-A' 0.7% against a 5% tolerance. About 36 minutes off the tier's bound. 351/351 tests pass in all three passes and sanitizer reports are 0 throughout. ⚠️ PEAK RSS IS THE REASON THIS COULD NOT BE DECIDED BEFORE, AND IT IS NOW MEASURED: 1.53 -> 3.84 GiB (+151%), which is 24% of the runner's 15.99 GiB. Ample, and the comparison that matters is linux-clang-libc++-asan at 27.7% — this lane is the lighter of the two. The figure is the same QUANTITY as the Linux lanes (a sum of per-process resident memory over the concurrent tree), taken by the job-object path in ci/measure-peak-rss.py; status=ok on all three passes, 16919/7234/16800 samples, denied_procs=0. ⚠️ A single test binary here peaks at 1.13 GiB, so peak_procs (4 -> 8) is the load-bearing check that the walk found the whole tree — a size band alone cannot tell a full tree from one big process. ⚠️ Summed test time rises 53.8%: this lane finishes sooner and spends more runner-minutes doing it. That is worth it ON the critical path and nowhere else, and it is the axis linux-clang-tsan failed on while its wall clock looked flat. See research/G19-fix-fpml-iso20022/decisions/speckit/267-widening-decisions.md §3b.
